title: Atacama dry ore-sorter: straintronic FeGa magnet, cryogenic aerosol cleans
idea: An Atacama miner sorts ore with sensors and air instead of water flotation. A Galfenol (FeGa) nanomagnet on a sputtered AlN piezo layer flips its easy axis under a ~0.2 V strain pulse (no current) and is read through a tunnel junction. Cryogenic argon/nitrogen aerosol jets remove particles in place of megasonic water scrubs.
why: Attojoule voltage-strain writes (fact 10), non-volatile storage (fact 3) and no rare earths. Dry aerosol cleaning cuts water by more than 10x.

title: Sub-damage-threshold direct-tunneling charge trap with volatile retention
idea: Store ~500 electrons in a nitride layer whose traps are engineered ~0.9 eV deep behind a 1.6 nm SiO2 tunnel oxide, written by direct tunneling at <2 V. Electrons never exceed the ~2-3 eV hot-carrier energy that generates oxide defects, and thermal emission gives ~0.5 s retention at 85 C (~100 s at 25 C), matched to refresh.
why: Flash wear-out is hot-carrier defect generation, so staying below that energy aims at >1e15 cycles. Gives a capacitorless ~4F2 1T cell with no pillar (facts 1, 4).

title: Ultra-wide-gap amorphous Ga2O3 storage node holding 0.1 fF for hours
idea: Generation leakage scales as ni ~ exp(-Eg/2kT), so moving from IGZO (3.2 eV) to RT-sputtered a-Ga2O3 (4.8 eV) cuts intrinsic generation by ~1e13. A 0.1 fF planar MIM node behind an a-Ga2O3 access device then holds a 0.3 V signal for >1e4 s, read by a local gain transistor.
why: Shrinks the capacitor ~50x (fact 1) and removes refresh (fact 3) in a planar BEOL-stackable cell, going beyond the IGZO prior work. The risk is defect-limited (not intrinsic) leakage in amorphous films.

title: Grow, don't etch: VLS nanowire electrodes at 150:1 aspect ratio
idea: Reverse subtractive to additive: Al or Sn catalyst dots on each storage node grow vertical silicon nanowire electrodes by vapor-liquid-solid growth (150:1 is easy to grow and impossible to etch), then ALD high-k and a conformal top electrode wrap them.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): the AR ~115 needed for more charge is reached without aspect-ratio-dependent etch limits, ~8 fF per cell; risk is catalyst contamination and wire placement.

title: Kilopass VLT thyristor fixed in GaN: standby current vanishes when hot
idea: T-RAM and Kilopass's VLT thyristor DRAM died because latch holding and leakage currents scale with the intrinsic carrier density ni, which explodes at high temperature in silicon. Grow the vertical p-n-p-n in GaN-on-Si (Eg 3.4 eV, ni ~1e-10 cm-3): off-state leakage and holding-current drift sit many orders of magnitude below silicon at 125 C while the cell stays a ~4F2 static latch.
why: Refresh-free static cell at Grade 1 temperature with negligible standby power; uses existing 300 mm GaN-on-Si lines.

title: Ferroelectric as backup, not primary: dual-mode DRAM/FeRAM capacitor
idea: Reverse the ferroelectric's role: run a PZT or SBT capacitor (1990s FeRAM process, 0.35-0.18 um) as a plain DRAM cell below its coercive voltage during active use, and switch polarization only to park a row when it goes idle, so idle rows need no refresh at all.
why: Refresh power (fact 3): idle rows draw zero refresh while active rows keep DRAM endurance; polarization switches only once per idle event (~1e9 lifetime); ready for old-node fabs.

title: Thermal-battery superionic gate freezes ions for perfect retention
idea: Adapt military thermal batteries whose electrolyte is solid (zero self-discharge) until heated: store the bit as Ag+ position in an Ag2S/AgI film that is superionic only above ~150 C; a ns Joule pulse unlocks the ion sublattice to write, and ions freeze in place on cooling.
why: 10x at same cost: a two-terminal element in a vertical 32-word-plane array sharing one hole litho, with no refresh; retention and write speed decoupled by the phase change.

title: Plated-wire space heritage: sell rad-hard magnetic memory first, then scale
idea: Plated wire flew on Voyager and the Shuttle because radiation cannot upset it. Launch a revived plated-wire-style magnetic memory on existing U.S. 200-mm trailing-node fabs into space and defense, where rad-hard memory sells at ~1000x DRAM $/bit, and use the margin to fund density learning toward commodity parts.
why: Funds a new storage element without a $15B fab, builds U.S. manufacturing know-how, and de-risks the physics on paying customers.

title: Diamond cutter: hydrogen-diamond floating-island cell, dry plasma-polished
idea: A diamond cutter polishes stone on a dry scaife. Build the storage node on hydrogen-terminated CVD diamond (5.5 eV gap), where a MoO3 acceptor layer makes a hole-doped channel and the node has almost no thermal leakage, so charge stays for years. Dry plasma/ICP polishing planarizes the diamond.
why: Refresh-free (fact 3), radiation-hard, and made of carbon rather than a chokepoint material. Dry polishing and dry etch give more than 10x less water.

title: Dealloyed nanoporous ruthenium sponge as the storage electrode
idea: Adapt tantalum-capacitor porous sintered anodes and catalyst dealloying: deposit a Ru-Al alloy plug in each storage hole, selectively leach the Al to leave a 3-5 nm-ligament Ru sponge, then ALD a 2 nm high-k and a conformal counter electrode through the pores.
why: Fact 1: internal surface is 5-8x the plain cylinder wall, so ~5 fF fits in AR ~20 holes instead of 60-75; shallower holes cut etch steps and pillar-collapse yield loss.

title: Raney-nickel sponge electrode: dealloy Ni-Al to multiply capacitor area
idea: Use the way Raney nickel catalyst is made. Deposit Ni-Al alloy in each shallow cup and leach the Al out with NaOH, leaving a nanoporous Ni sponge with ~5 nm ligaments that ALD then coats with Al2O3/ZrO2 dielectric and a TiN counter electrode.
why: Fact 1: 10-20x internal area per footprint makes 5 fF at AR ~5. Ni, Al, Zr, Ti and O replace Ru, Hf and W electrodes and liners.

title: Luthier's arched top: bistable pre-stressed buckled nanobeam bit
idea: A violin maker knows that an arched, pre-stressed plate snaps between two stable shapes. A 200 nm compressively stressed SiN/TiN nanobeam is buckled either up or down; an electrostatic pulse snaps it over and a capacitive readout senses its shape, with zero standby power and no charge to leak.
why: A non-volatile mechanical state removes refresh (fact 3) and row hammer (fact 9: no charge coupling between rows); elastic snapping of amorphous films has no intrinsic wear-out mechanism, so the target is >1e15 cycles.

title: Radiation-proof snap-through buckled nanobeam holds bit mechanically
idea: Satellite memory must ignore single-event upsets, so a 200 nm compressively pre-stressed SiN or TiN beam is buckled up or down; an electrostatic pulse snaps it between the two stable shapes in ~5-20 ns and a capacitive readout senses its position. There is no stored charge for a heavy ion to disturb and standby power is zero.
why: Non-volatile, rad-immune, BEOL-compatible bit with no capacitor wall (fact 1) and no refresh (fact 3); nanobeam endurance beyond 1e12 cycles and stiction are risks, density ~10-20F2 initially.

title: Niobium-oxide cell with self-healing solid-electrolyte top plate
idea: TRIZ #22 Blessing in disguise: copy the solid niobium electrolytic capacitor. Anodize a Nb storage electrode to Nb2O5 (k~40) and use a MnO2 or conductive-polymer top plate; at any leakage hot spot the fault current itself converts MnO2 to insulating Mn2O3 (or de-dopes the polymer), sealing the defect, and an in-field 're-forming' pulse regrows thinned oxide by anodization.
why: Fact 1: k~40 with self-sealed defect tail lets the dielectric run ~30% thinner (Cs +30-50%); repair is built into the storage element.

title: Charge-gated Mott channel amplifies a few hundred stored electrons
idea: Effect walk: filling-controlled Mott transition. The storage node gates a 3-nm channel of a correlated oxide (strained NdNiO3 or electron-doped Sr2IrO4) poised at its metal-insulator boundary, so a few hundred stored electrons (~0.1-0.3 e per unit cell under a 100 nm2 gate) swing channel resistance ~100x for a gain read.
why: Cuts required storage charge ~100x (5 fF to ~0.03-0.05 fF), removing the high-AR capacitor (fact 1) and shrinking the cell toward 4F2; risks are retaining so few electrons against the leakage tail and Mott-channel variability.

title: Swap stored charge for conducting ferroelectric domain wall presence
idea: In thin-film LiNbO3 or BiFeO3 mesa cells, the bit is whether a charged, conducting domain wall bridges two side electrodes. Writing creates or erases the wall in ns, and reading senses wall conduction (on/off >10^4) without switching polarization.
why: Non-destructive read cuts the restore share of the ~5.9 pJ/bit destructive read (fact 8); non-volatile, so no refresh (fact 3); cycling above 10^10 has been reported.

title: Po: the bit is a rattle — ion-in-cage endohedral fullerene dipole
idea: Po: the bit is a rattle in a box. Extracted: a Li+@C60 endohedral molecule has two off-centre sites for the lithium ion; a field pushes the ion to one side, forming a molecular dipole that shifts the threshold of an adjacent 2D-channel transistor, while the cage stops the ion from ever migrating.
why: ~1 nm bits with no lattice ion migration (no wear). The room-temperature barrier between sites is speculative.

title: Van der Waals stiction latch: nanoflap stays stuck until kicked
idea: Effect walk: van der Waals/Casimir adhesion. A 50-nm graphene or SiC nanoflap is pulled into contact by a ~0.5 V electrostatic pulse and held at zero power by vdW adhesion; a second electrode releases it, and a 10-mV contact-resistance check reads the state.
why: Zero hold power (no refresh), ~aJ contact reads at 10 mV and ~0.1 fJ actuation of an aF-scale gap put access energy >10x below DRAM; contact wear over >10^15 cycles is the reliability risk.

title: Swap voltage level for oscillation phase: nanoscale parametron bit
idea: Revive Goto's parametron at the nanoscale. Each cell is a nanomechanical or LC resonator pumped at 2f by a shared clock, the bit is the 0 or pi phase of its subharmonic oscillation (which the pump keeps locked), and the cell is read by phase comparison with a reference.
why: The bit is a binary phase, not a leaking charge, so there is no refresh (fact 3) and no charge-disturb row hammer (fact 9). Adiabatic quantum-flux-parametron versions at 4 K reach zJ switching.

title: Thermochromic-ink spin-crossover bit: Fe-triazole molecules hold spin state
idea: Borrow thermochromic ink printing: a film of [Fe(Htrz)2(trz)](BF4) spin-crossover complex (Fe, C, H, N, B, F) sits inside its room-temperature thermal hysteresis loop. A ns heat or field pulse flips molecules between high and low spin, and the ~10% volume and dielectric change is read capacitively or through a strain-gated channel.
why: Bistable molecular storage needing no refresh (fact 3), solution-printable from cents of iron and organics. Write energy is the latent heat of a 20 nm dot, ~fJ.

title: Series negative-capacitance layer that raises cell capacitance
idea: Reverse the series-capacitor rule: add a thin HZO ferroelectric biased into its negative-capacitance branch in series with the ZrO2/Al2O3 cell dielectric, so 1/C = 1/C_DE - 1/|C_FE| and total capacitance rises 2-3x above the dielectric alone while |C_FE| > C_DE keeps it hysteresis-free.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): acts like k ~70+ without new high-k chemistry, giving 5 fF at AR ~30 instead of 75; risk is stabilizing NC with multi-domain films.

title: Ceria oxygen buffer refillable like a catalytic converter's storage
idea: TRIZ #9 Prior anti-action: insert a ~0.5-nm CeO2 interlayer into the ZrO2 stack. As with the oxygen-storage capacity in car catalytic converters, Ce4+/Ce3+ swaps donate oxygen to fill vacancies formed under field stress, and a periodic thermal anneal pulls oxygen back from an RuO2/TiON electrode reservoir to recharge the buffer.
why: Facts 1 and 3: slows leakage-tail growth so thinner, higher-Cs dielectrics survive 10 years; a rechargeable buffer is repair by design.

title: Swiss-roll pastry: strain-released self-rolling capacitor stack
idea: Deposit a planar TiN/Al2O3-HfO2/TiN stack on a strained SiNx bilayer over a sacrificial layer; selective release lets the built-in strain roll it into a 3-5-turn microtube, multiplying capacitor area per footprint ~10x from planar deposition only, like rolling a Swiss roll.
why: Facts 1 and 2: 3D capacitance with no high-AR etch, a natural fit for lateral capacitors in horizontal 3D DRAM; demonstrated with sputter, ALD and wet release in university labs; shrinking roll diameters below ~1 um is the risk.

title: Sugar cube: croconic-acid proton ferroelectric replaces fluoropolymer PVDF
idea: Stimulus 'sugar cube' (a crystal of small organic molecules) -> vapor-deposit croconic acid, a hydrogen-bonded organic ferroelectric (~20 uC/cm^2, highest among organics) whose polarization flips by proton transfer along H-bonds, as the storage layer of a BEOL cell at <150 C. It replaces PVDF-TrFE, the standard organic ferroelectric, which is a fluoropolymer.
why: Low-temperature, fluorine-free nonvolatile storage layer that can be stacked over periphery in tiers (fact 2); proton-transfer switching is fast and low-voltage (fact 10).

title: Zone-refining domain walls: LiNbO3 conducting walls as nondestructive bits
idea: A zone-refining heater sweeps a molten zone through a bar. Here a short pulse sweeps a ferroelectric domain wall across a tiny single-crystal LiNbO3 mesa made by thin-film ion slicing. The bit is whether a conductive wall bridges the electrodes, read as a uA wall current without switching polarization.
why: Fact 8: read is nondestructive with a large current signal and no capacitor. Writes take <10 ns, and single-crystal film gives endurance far above HZO.

title: Self-healing ferroelectric nematic liquid in nano-wells, fatigue-free
idea: Thirty-year industrial controllers cannot tolerate ferroelectric fatigue, so polarization is held by a ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (P ~4-6 uC/cm2) sealed in nano-wells; being a fluid, pinned domains and defects anneal away, removing wake-up and fatigue. Surface anchoring gives two stable polar orientations, read by displacement charge or a coupled FET.
why: Promises effectively unlimited polarization endurance with ~5x the charge per area of a DRAM capacitor; switching (us today) must reach ~100 ns through nanoscale confinement.

title: Sliding ferroelectric bilayer flips by interlayer slip at 0.2 V
idea: Effect walk: sliding (stacking) ferroelectricity. In a parallel-stacked h-BN or 3R-MoS2 bilayer, the out-of-plane dipole reverses when one layer slides one bond length (AB to BA) under ~0.1-0.3 V, and a graphene-contacted tunnel junction reads the ~10x tunneling-resistance change non-destructively.
why: No ion displacement across the film and ~0.2 V on an atomically thin capacitor cut write energy ~25x versus 1-V CV2, and the non-destructive read removes restore energy (fact 8); reported fatigue-free switching suits the endurance target.

title: The wall is the bit: conducting domain walls in insulating ferroelectric
idea: Rearrange which part stores the data: in LiNbO3 or BiFeO3 films a domain wall conducts while domains insulate; a write creates or erases a wall across a 20 nm electrode gap, and a sub-coercive read senses the wall current without disturbing it.
why: Destructive read and refresh (facts 3,8): nonvolatile NDRO with uA read current and no restore write; 1-2 nm walls make density litho-limited, not charge-limited.

title: Barrier-trimmed MTJ trades ten-year retention for tenfold cheaper writes
idea: Effect walk: Neel-Arrhenius thermal activation. Design the MTJ free layer for thermal stability ~25-30 (seconds of retention at 85 C) instead of ~60 (ten years); critical current scales with the barrier, so writes need ~2-2.5x less current and, with shorter pulses, ~5-10x less energy, while a refresh every ~100 ms costs ~1% duty.
why: Turns MRAM's over-engineered retention into energy: a DRAM-class volatile cell from a mature MTJ stack at ~10x lower write energy than NVM-grade STT, with non-destructive read and no capacitor (fact 1).

title: Eliminate refresh: bistable tunnel-diode pair holds each bit statically
idea: Eliminate refresh: put two Si/SiGe resonant interband tunnel diodes in series on each storage node, so their negative-differential-resistance curves cross at two stable node voltages (a Goto-pair latch) with ~pA standby current per cell, while one access transistor reads and writes as in DRAM. The diodes are grown by RPCVD in hydrogen carrier with in-situ B/P delta doping, so no rare gases are used.
why: A static cell with a 1T footprint plus a vertical diode stack drives refresh energy and bandwidth loss (fact 3) to zero and needs only a small capacitor (fact 1); risk is peak-to-valley ratio uniformity at nm scale.

title: Coulomb-blockade nanodot bit: ten electrons, held by charging energy
idea: Scarcity rule: the bit gets 1000x less charge. Self-assembled 2 nm Si dots in the gate oxide store 5-10 electrons each, and their Coulomb charging energy (>10 kT) blocks back-tunneling so retention comes from electrostatics rather than oxide thickness; a sensitive gain transistor reads the threshold shift.
why: Shrinks stored charge from ~30,000 to ~10 electrons, deleting the capacitor (fact 1) and cutting write energy ~1000x (fact 10); room-temperature blockade needs tight dot uniformity.

title: Shape-memory twin variants open or close a tunnel gap
idea: Effect walk: ferroelastic martensitic twinning. A 20-nm NiTi nano-pillar has two stable twin variants whose heights differ by ~4% (~0.8 nm); a piezo or thermal pulse selects the variant, opening or closing a ~1-nm h-BN/vacuum tunnel gap above it, which changes tunneling current by up to ~10^6-10^7.
why: A crystallographic barrier holds the state with zero leakage and no refresh, and the enormous read margin enables tiny-swing reads; abundant Ni and Ti (no W); nanoscale martensite fatigue over 10^15 cycles is unknown.

title: Photographic latent-image bit: few silver atoms hold a few electrons
idea: Silver-halide film keeps a stable 4-atom Ag cluster as the latent image, which development later amplifies. Here sub-3 nm Ag clusters self-assembled in an oxide each hold 1-5 electrons behind a Coulomb-blockade barrier. An integrated single-electron transistor 'develops' the latent charge on read.
why: Fact 1: about 5 electrons replace 5 fF (~30k electrons), cutting write charge and CV2 energy ~1000x. The high charging energy makes tunneling-out, and so refresh, rare.

title: Pottery glaze: nanoscale barrier-layer giant-k capacitor dielectric
idea: Stimulus 'glazed pottery' (conductive body, insulating skin) -> build the dielectric from 3-5 nm oxygen-deficient TiO2-x grains each wrapped in a ~1 nm Al2O3 skin by alternating chloride/organometallic ALD; charge piles up at the many thin internal barriers (the CaCu3Ti4O12 trick) for an effective k of several hundred.
why: Exceeds the k~70 needed (fact 1), allowing near-planar capacitors with AR <20:1 and fewer deep-etch steps (fact 4); fluorine-free chemistry.

title: Altermagnet tunnel junction: magnetoresistance without stray fields
idea: Scarcity rule: no net magnetization allowed, since stray fields set MRAM pitch. Store the bit in the Neel vector of an altermagnet (RuO2, MnTe or Mn5Si3) whose spin-split bands still give tunneling magnetoresistance, and flip it with spin-splitter or spin-orbit torque at THz-class dynamics.
why: 10 nm-pitch magnetic bits with no dipolar crosstalk, ps writes and unlimited endurance (density and energy axes); room-temperature TMR magnitude is unproven.

title: Buried germanium quantum well confines holes without any p-n junction
idea: Invert 'retention is set by junction leakage' -> set it by a band offset. Holes are stored in a compressively strained Ge quantum well 5 nm below a Si channel; the ~0.5 eV valence-band offset confines them with no p-n junction, so the defect-driven GIDL/junction tail becomes designed thermionic escape with retention ~exp(dEv/kT).
why: Capacitorless 4F^2 vertical cell (fact 1) whose retention is set by epitaxy rather than random defects, tightening the leakage tail and cutting refresh (fact 3).

title: Deliberately imperfect bits: shorter capacitors for AI tensor mantissas
idea: Worsen: insist every bit of every byte meet 1e-15 error at worst-case retention. Flip: build a tolerant cell class with ~40% less capacitor height for neural-network weights and activations; sign and exponent bits live in full cells while low-order mantissa bits live in short cells refreshed rarely.
why: Cuts capacitor etch time, AR and refresh for the AI data that dominates demand (facts 1, 3, 4): ~20-30% lower cost per bit on that tier.

title: Bubble memory without the shift register: one garnet bubble per cell
idea: Magnetic bubble memory died from serial millisecond access and external rotating-field coils. Pattern ~40 nm insulating TmIG garnet dots under a Pt strip: a spin-orbit-torque pulse nucleates or annihilates one bubble domain in place, and spin-Hall magnetoresistance in the same Pt reads it, so nothing moves and no tunnel barrier exists to wear out.
why: Random access in ~10 ns, nonvolatile (zero refresh), no barrier breakdown so endurance is not oxide-limited; insulating magnet means no electromigration. Risk: small SMR read signal.

title: Noncollinear antiferromagnet bits pack tight with zero stray field
idea: Effect walk: spin Hall switching + anomalous Hall effect in a Weyl antiferromagnet. 10-nm Mn3Sn islands store the bit as the chirality of their triangular spin order, switched by spin-orbit torque from an adjacent line and read by the sign of the large anomalous Hall voltage they emit despite near-zero net moment.
why: Zero stray field removes inter-cell magnetic disturb so pitch can approach 2F, and dynamics reach 10-100 ps; Mn and Sn are abundant; aims at density and endurance beyond MRAM's dipolar limit.

title: Altermagnet bits read by spin-split tunneling with zero net moment
idea: Invert 'magnetic memory needs net magnetization to be read' -> store the bit in an altermagnet whose moments cancel. MnTe or RuO2-class altermagnets have zero net moment yet spin-split bands, so a tunnel junction reads Neel orientation by TMR and spin-splitter torque writes it; no stray field permits ~10 nm pitch and wear-free, THz-fast switching.
why: Non-volatile, unlimited endurance, dense without dipolar crosstalk and immune to row-hammer-style disturbance (fact 9); MnTe avoids ruthenium scarcity; room-temperature TMR magnitude is the risk.

title: Kinetic-inductance nanowire loops storing single flux quanta at 4 K
idea: Store each bit as the presence or absence of one flux quantum (Phi0 = 2.07e-15 Wb) in a loop of 20 nm NbN nanowire. Huge kinetic inductance keeps beta_L = 2*pi*L*Ic/Phi0 > 1 in a ~100 nm loop, the persistent current never decays, and a nanocryotron reads it.
why: Zero leakage and write energy ~Ic*Phi0 ~ 1e-19 J, ~1000x below DRAM. Aimed at cryogenic AI and quantum-control racks; density is set by loop inductance, not capacitor charge (facts 1, 3, 10).

title: Flux quanta in kinetic-inductance nanowire loops for cryogenic AI memory
idea: Effect walk: flux quantization in superconductors. Each bit is the presence or absence of one flux quantum in a loop of 10-nm-wide NbN or NbTiN nanowire whose large kinetic inductance shrinks the loop to ~0.1 um2; writes and reads use nanocryotron (nTron) switches instead of Josephson junctions, costing ~10^-18 J per access.
why: Access energy ~10^-18 J vs ~10^-14 J for DRAM cell+bitline: even after a ~500x 4-K cooling penalty it remains ~20x lower, giving cryogenic accelerators and quantum-control stacks a missing dense memory.

title: Thermostat-held VO2 phase bits in hysteresis window
idea: Couple chip and datacenter scales: hold the die by liquid cooling at the middle of a W-doped VO2 thermal hysteresis window, where both metal and insulator phases are stable; Joule pulses set metal and Peltier micro-coolers reset insulator.
why: Endurance and speed: ns electronic phase change without atomic migration; the facility cooling loop becomes part of the memory.

title: Eliminate up-down polarization: polar-vortex chirality bits in oxide superlattices
idea: Eliminate the up/down polarization picture: in PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattices, polarization curls into vortices or polar skyrmions whose handedness is a topologically protected bit, written by a curl-shaped field from split electrodes and read through its chirality-dependent (gyrotropic) electrical response.
why: Topological protection gives nonvolatility with no net polarization reversal (low fatigue) and ~10-nm bits; attacks refresh (fact 3) and density; electrical chirality readout is unproven.

title: Potter's wheel: polar vortex chirality in PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattices
idea: A potter knows that a pot thrown clockwise looks the same as one thrown counter-clockwise until you feel the spiral. In PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattices the polarization curls into ~10 nm vortices whose handedness (chirality) a field can switch; it is read optically or through resistance coupled to the piezoresponse.
why: A topologically protected state that stays stable at sizes where ordinary ferroelectrics depolarize (facts 1, 3). The lead content is a drawback.

title: Light-powered self-refreshing photo-latch cell under an LED flood
idea: MAGNIFY the refresh source from a controller to photons: each cell adds a tiny photodiode feeding its storage node through a transistor gated by that node, so under uniform LED illumination '1' nodes keep topping themselves up while '0' nodes stay shut, a bistable cell needing no refresh commands; built on a CIS MPW.
why: Removes refresh commands and the 10-20% bandwidth tax (fact 3); the photocurrent needed only has to beat ~13 fA, so LED power is negligible.

title: Pumped-hydro twin reservoirs: fixed electron shuttled between paired quantum dots
idea: Like pumped hydro moving the same water between two reservoirs, each cell holds a fixed electron that never leaves the cell, only shifting between two coupled 2-4-nm Si nanodots (~0.3 eV charging energy) across a tunnel barrier; a write gate tilts the double well and an electrometer gate senses which dot is occupied.
why: Facts 3 and 8: with no path to a bitline there is no junction leakage to refresh, and read is non-destructive (no restore after 128x overfetch); RT operation needs sub-5-nm dots with uniform barriers, the key risk.

title: Neuron's resting potential: nanobattery bit read as open-circuit voltage
idea: A biologist notes that neurons hold state as an ion gradient behind closed channels, not as electrostatic charge. Each cell is a ~10 nm solid-state Li-ion couple (LixCoO2 / LiPON / Si) whose state of charge sets a 0.3 V or 0.6 V open-circuit potential; a ns current pulse through a selector writes it and a high-impedance sense FET reads it.
why: Bypasses the capacitor charge wall: intercalation stores orders of magnitude more charge per volume than a dielectric, and an electrochemical potential does not drain through the access-transistor tail, so refresh largely disappears (facts 1, 3). The risk is ns-scale ion kinetics.

title: Bulk photovoltaic read: polarization reports its sign as photocurrent
idea: Effect walk: bulk photovoltaic (shift-current) effect. Ferroelectric nano-capacitors (BaTiO3 or CuInP2S6) under a shared transparent electrode are flood-illuminated by a backside waveguide flash; each cell's photocurrent sign equals its polarization direction, integrated by a per-column gain stage without switching the domain.
why: Non-destructive ferroelectric read removes FeRAM's read-then-rewrite fatigue and restore energy (fact 8), letting polar cells act as working memory with unlimited reads; shift currents are small, so sensing gain is the risk.

title: Swiss-roll capacitor: self-rolled film-capacitor winding inside each cell
idea: Copy how wound film capacitors are made, at nanoscale. Deposit a strained TiN/ZrO2/TiN/ZrO2 nanomembrane on a sacrificial layer and release it, so built-in stress rolls it into a 3-4 turn spiral tube standing in the cell. Each winding adds electrode area without etching a 70:1 hole.
why: Facts 1 and 4: a stress-driven roll replaces the costly high-AR capacitor etch. Target is 5 fF at an equivalent AR of ~20.

title: MLCC-in-a-pillar: tape-cast style Ni/BaTiO3 multilayer cell capacitor
idea: Shrink multilayer ceramic capacitor (MLCC) manufacturing into each cell. A pillar holds 20 alternating Ni/BaTiO3 5 nm layers, like co-fired MLCC sheets, with odd layers recessed on one sidewall and even layers on the other, so a storage-node contact and a plate contact each reach every other electrode.
why: Fact 1: 6 fF from a pillar of AR ~7 instead of 70, using only Ni, Ba, Ti and O. MLCC makers already co-process Ni/BaTiO3 at enormous volume.

title: Rock-candy croconic acid: proton-hopping organic ferroelectric bit
idea: Like rock candy growing on a seeded string, croconic acid (C5H2O5) crystallizes from vapor onto seed lines between TiN electrodes. It is a room-temperature ferroelectric whose polarization flips by proton transfer along hydrogen bonds, read through a ferroelectric tunnel junction.
why: ~20 uC/cm2 polarization from C, H and O alone, with low coercive field (targets fact 10's voltage floor). Proton tautomerism has no oxygen-vacancy fatigue path.

title: Gate-leakage load latch: engineered leakage holds static bits
idea: MAGNIFY a parasitic into the mechanism: in a 2-transistor cell on thin-oxide foundry devices, gate-tunneling current of one transistor acts as a pA pull-up and subthreshold current of the other as pull-down; sized so their I-V curves cross three times, the node has two stable voltages and holds statically.
why: No refresh (fact 3) at roughly half the area of 6T SRAM, designable on a 65/28 nm MPW; tight process variation control is required.

title: Swap SiO2 tunnel barrier for InAs/AlSb resonant triple barrier
idea: Store charge on an InAs floating gate isolated by an InAs/AlSb triple-barrier resonant-tunnelling structure (ULTRARAM-style). At about 2.5 V the resonance aligns and electrons tunnel quickly at low energy; at 0 V the 2.1 eV AlSb conduction-band offset blocks them, so retention exceeds years.
why: A non-volatile, DRAM-speed cell with endurance above 10^7 already shown, ~100x lower switching energy per area than DRAM, and no refresh (fact 3); it is grown on Si by MBE, a tool set available in the U.S.

title: Lithium niobate domain-wall conduction gives nondestructive reads
idea: Scale down to 1 nm domain walls: in wafer-bonded single-crystal LiNbO3 films a written ferroelectric domain creates a conducting wall between electrodes, so the bit is read by current without switching.
why: Destructive read and endurance: nondestructive read, 1e10+ cycles, single-crystal film from mature RF-filter wafers.

title: Cr2O3 magnetoelectric memory's 34 C Neel point swapped for BiFeO3
idea: Voltage-controlled exchange-bias memories built on Cr2O3 stalled because its Neel temperature (~307 K) is below normal operation, let alone 125 C. Use La-doped BiFeO3 (TN ~640 K, Tc ~1100 K): a 100-200 mV pulse switches its ferroelectric polarization, which rotates the antiferromagnetic axis and, through exchange, a CoFe free layer read by an MTJ.
why: ~1 fJ current-free writes with magnetic order stable at 125 C/10 y; a nonvolatile DRAM-class cell in MESO style.

title: Self-healing clearing electrodes burn out capacitor weak spots at test
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): the die must look like normal DDR5, so fix the leakage tail inside the cell. Make the capacitor top electrode an ultrathin clearable layer, as in metallized-film capacitors: a wafer-sort overvoltage pulse makes each dielectric weak spot conduct and locally oxidizes or vaporizes the electrode around it, isolating the defect so the dielectric can be thinned ~20%.
why: ~20% more Cs from a thinner dielectric (fact 1) and a tighter retention tail (fact 3) with no interface change; each cleared area must stay below ~5% of the electrode.

title: Seed-pulled single-crystal SrTiO3 capacitor via lateral epitaxial overgrowth
idea: Borrow Czochralski seeding. Open a window to a single-crystal SrRuO3 seed and grow SrTiO3 laterally over the bottom electrode as one crystal, the way GaN is overgrown laterally, instead of as a fine-grained film. Removing grain boundaries removes leakage paths and suppresses the dead layer that holds polycrystalline STO to k~100.
why: Fact 1: k of ~250-300 in 8 nm films is 5-6x today's ZrO2. Capacitor AR could drop from ~70:1 to ~15:1.

title: Widrow memistor reborn as a protonic WO3 three-terminal BEOL gain cell
idea: Widrow's 1960 memistor stored a value as electroplated copper thickness on a resistive film read through separate terminals. Build a three-terminal protonic cell (WO3 channel, ZrO2:H electrolyte, Pd gate) in the BEOL of an existing 180/130-nm fab; write pulses move H+ in or out and the channel conductance is read without disturbing it.
why: Separated read path means no read disturb (Fact 8), hour retention (Fact 3), fJ writes below 1 V (Fact 10); ~1e9 endurance makes it a weight/state tier rather than general DRAM; BEOL-only on U.S. 200-mm fabs.

title: Conductive ferroelectric domain walls in thin-film lithium niobate
idea: Combine the thin-film lithium niobate photonics platform with domain-wall nanoelectronics: a voltage writes or erases a charged domain wall between two electrodes, and the wall conducts 1e3-1e6x more than the bulk crystal. Read is a small non-destructive current through the wall, and the polarization holds the bit with no refresh.
why: Zero refresh plus non-destructive read (fact 8); LiNbO3 domain walls show >1e10-cycle endurance and fast switching; U.S. TFLN foundries exist.

title: Persistent current instead of leaky charge: niobium flux-loop memory
idea: Reverse decay into perpetuity: each bit is a single flux quantum circulating in a superconducting niobium loop built with the 1990s Nb/AlOx/Nb trilayer process (1-2 um junctions) at 4 K, where current flows forever without refresh; a Josephson junction switches on read depending on loop current.
why: Energy (facts 3,5): ~1e-19 J switching and zero static loss, the natural partner for cryogenic accelerators; density is poor (~10 um2/bit), so the gain is energy, not cost.

title: Single-photon avalanche diode logic: Geiger-mode read of a 300-electron node
idea: Treat the storage node as a gate over a tiny Geiger-mode avalanche junction: the stored charge shifts local breakdown by ~0.3 V, and the read biases between the two breakdown voltages for ~2 ns so a self-quenched avalanche (a large digital pulse) fires only for one state, as in SPAD pixels.
why: Fact 1: digital-gain sensing needs ~0.2-0.5 fF instead of ~5 fF, collapsing capacitor height 10-20x; dark-count false fires (~1e-7 per ns window) and afterpulsing demand ECC and are the risk.

title: Superconducting flux-trap cell taped out on an existing shuttle
idea: Worsen: assume new memory needs a new fab and billions. Flip: store bits as single flux quanta in kinetic-inductance NbN loops, taped out on an existing superconducting-electronics foundry shuttle (~$50-100k per run) and tested in a ~$250k cryocooler, targeting a 1e5-cell array for cryogenic AI datacentres.
why: aJ writes, zero static power, unlimited endurance (facts 3, 5, 10) with no new fab.

title: Ramtron FeRAM read without destroying: second-harmonic polarization sensing
idea: Ramtron FeRAM was hobbled by destructive reads that forced a write-back on every access and drove fatigue. Read instead with a small sub-coercive AC tone (~0.2 Vc): the sign of the capacitor's second-harmonic current, from its asymmetric C-V curvature, flips with polarization direction, so a lock-in style sense amp reads the bit without switching it.
why: Non-destructive read removes write-back energy and read fatigue (Fact 8): ~2-5x lower read energy and effectively unlimited read endurance.

title: Sputtered AlScN ferroelectric cap with 20x hafnia's charge
idea: Worsen: depend on ALD precursors and hafnia wake-up cycling. Flip: use a used reactive-sputter tool (~$400k) to deposit 10 nm wurtzite AlScN on 200 mm CMOS back-end test chips and use its ~100 uC/cm2 polarization as a planar storage capacitor with no deep trench; 24 months maps endurance and scaling.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): ~20x charge per area versus a linear dielectric in a planar cap at low capital; endurance is the risk to retire.

title: Po: memory that remembers by bending — bistable SiC nanobridge
idea: Po: memory that remembers by bending. Extracted: a compressively prestrained SiC nanobridge buckles up or down; an electrostatic pulse snaps it through, its position changes a capacitance read by the bitline, and stiff contact-free SiC (no stiction) targets >1e15 cycles.
why: Zero leakage and zero standby (fact 3) with aJ snap energy (fact 10). Fatigue at 1e15 cycles is unproven.

title: Single femtosecond pulse toggles ferrimagnet bit: light-written magnetic memory
idea: Effect walk: helicity-independent all-optical switching in ferrimagnets. A 10-nm GdFeCo (or rare-earth-free Mn-based ferrimagnet) free layer of an MTJ sits under a plasmonic nano-antenna fed by a waveguide; each ~100-fs pulse deterministically toggles magnetization through ultrafast sublattice demagnetization, and TMR reads it electrically.
why: Picosecond writes with no current through the junction (unlimited write endurance), and optical addressing removes wordline-driver periphery (fact 7); Gd supply concentration and nanoscale plasmonic coupling efficiency are the risks.

title: Eliminate metal electrodes: degenerate epitaxial silicon plates replace TiN and tungsten
idea: Eliminate sputtered TiN and tungsten electrodes: form both capacitor plates and node contacts from in-situ phosphorus-doped (>1e21 cm-3) epitaxial Si or SiGe grown with hydrogen carrier, so there are no metal targets, no argon PVD and no tungsten; at that doping the depletion penalty is under ~5% of capacitance.
why: Removes a tungsten dependence (China ~80%) and argon PVD chambers (scarce-resource axis), and same-tool epitaxy cuts steps; risks are plate resistance slowing RC and depletion at high field.

title: CCD-loop memory: charge packets circulate, no per-bit contact
idea: Scarcity rule: no transistor or contact per bit. Bits ride as charge packets in buried-channel CCD loops of 64 cells clocked by 2-phase gates, and one sense-and-regenerate stage per loop reads and restores each packet as it passes, so a bit costs only ~2F2 of gate pitch.
why: Removes per-bit transistors and contacts (fact 4) for ~3x density at the same F; buried-channel dark current gives seconds of retention; the ~32-clock average wait adds latency.

title: Borax box: boron-aluminum nitride ferroelectric from U.S. boron, no scandium
idea: Stimulus 'borax laundry box' (mined in Boron, California) -> sputter wurtzite Al(1-x)B(x)N ferroelectric (remanent polarization ~100 uC/cm^2, ~5-10x HZO) from Al/B targets in N2/Ar and pattern it with Cl2/BCl3; use it as a planar storage capacitor or ferroelectric gate. No hafnium, scandium or fluorine.
why: ~10x charge per area enables a planar storage element (fact 1) built from abundant domestic boron and aluminum (scarce-resource and U.S. manufacturability axes).

title: Fatigue-free sliding ferroelectric bilayers built by tear-and-stack
idea: Worsen: assume a new storage material needs a fab to evaluate. Flip: with a ~$300k glovebox and transfer stage, tear-and-stack parallel bilayer hBN or 3R-MoS2 whose polarization flips by interlayer sliding (no ion motion), and spend 24 months proving 1e12+ cycles and 10 ns switching on 100-device arrays.
why: An endurance-unlimited, atomically thin polarization bit (facts 1, 3); de-risks a new storage physics for under $1M.

title: Swap per-bit access transistors for vertical CCD charge-packet strings
idea: Reuse the 3D NAND stack: each vertical poly or IGZO channel works as a CCD in which the 128 tier gates, clocked in three phases, shift ~40 charge packets up and down to a regenerating sense amplifier at the top. There is no contact, capacitor or access transistor per bit, and each pass through the amplifier refreshes the packet.
why: ~1 bit per 250 nm2 (better than 864 nm2 for 6F2) using only DUV 3D NAND tools (facts 2, 4, 7); no tunnelling, so endurance is unlimited; average shift latency is ~20 ns.

title: Diatom biomineralization: DNA-origami templates place 10-nm storage nodes
idea: Diatoms grow silica shells on protein templates; adsorb DNA-origami tiles carrying metal seeds on a 10-nm grid onto shape-matched landing sites defined by relaxed e-beam litho, then grow storage nodes or floating islands from the seeds by ALD or electroless plating, burning off the origami afterward.
why: Fact 4: sub-12-nm feature placement without EUV using wet chemistry plus one relaxed-pitch e-beam step, all university-buildable; placement yield (~95-99% today versus >99.9999% needed) requires spare rows and ECC.

title: Nanoimprinted sol-gel high-k cup capacitors on roll-to-roll polymer web
idea: Invert 'capacitor geometry is defined by lithography plus etch' -> stamp it. A reusable master with 30 nm x 600 nm pillars imprints cup cavities into spin-on TiO2/BaTiO3 sol-gel on polyimide web, then ALD electrodes coat them, replacing EUV and HAR plasma etch with mechanical replication at metres per minute.
why: Cuts masks, EUV and capacitor-module capex >10x (fact 4) with roll-to-roll throughput for cost/bit; AR-20 demolding defects and overlay to the TFT layer are the risks.

title: Polarization-built well: GaN 2DEG pocket holds charge for hours
idea: Reverse doping-defined wells for polarization-defined ones: in AlGaN/GaN the built-in polarization makes an electron well with no dopants; a gated, isolated 2DEG pocket stores electrons behind a 3.4 eV-gap barrier and an adjacent HEMT channel senses it, using 0.25-0.5 um GaN RF fab tools.
why: Leakage (fact 3) and U.S. manufacturability: wide gap and epitaxial barriers target hours of retention in existing U.S. defense GaN fabs; risk is trap-driven charge drift (current collapse).

title: Sailor's storm-proof compass: antiferromagnet Neel-vector bit
idea: A sailor wants a compass that no passing magnet can deflect. Store the bit in the Neel vector of an antiferromagnet (CuMnAs or Mn3Sn), switched by a picosecond current pulse through spin-orbit torque and read through anisotropic or anomalous Hall resistance.
why: Non-volatile, immune to stray fields, switching at THz rates, with no row-hammer coupling and no MTJ stack (facts 3, 9).

title: Vertical charge-coupled shift-register strings replace per-cell transistors
idea: MAGNIFY charge transfer and MINIFY contacts: bits are charge packets clocked along vertical poly-Si CCD channels formed in 3D-NAND-style holes with 64 gate tiers; each string has one inject/sense contact at the top, so storage sites need no access transistor or capacitor.
why: 3D stacking with a NAND-like process (fact 2) and much less periphery (fact 7); average latency ~32 shifts x 0.5 ns = 16 ns, needs charge-transfer inefficiency < 1e-5.

title: Built-in-bias antiferroelectric ZrO2 minor-loop dynamic polarization cell
idea: ALD ZrO2 crystallizes antiferroelectric at <=350 C. Asymmetric TiN/RuO2 electrodes (~0.5 eV work-function offset) shift the double loop so zero bias sits inside one lobe, and the field-induced ferroelectric state stores the '1', relaxing over a designed ~1 s with no wake-up or imprint fatigue.
why: 2-3x the charge per area of a linear dielectric (fact 1) with antiferroelectric endurance >1e12. A refreshable volatile ferroic store at BEOL temperature.

title: Work-function-offset antiferroelectric gives two zero-bias states for pacemakers
idea: Pacemakers need memory that idles at zero power for ten years; one added mask patterns a high-work-function RuO2 top electrode (vs TiN) over ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric capacitors, shifting one double-hysteresis loop so two polarization states coexist at 0 V. Antiferroelectric switching avoids HZO wake-up and offers 1e12+ endurance.
why: Non-volatile, refresh-free capacitor in the existing cell geometry for one mask (fact 3); read remains destructive but refresh energy and standby power vanish.

title: Po: a magnet with no magnetization — chiral antiferromagnet Mn3Sn bit
idea: Po: a magnet with no magnetization. Extracted: store the bit in the octupole order of a chiral antiferromagnet (Mn3Sn), switched by spin-orbit torque from a BiSb topological-insulator line (no Pt/W) and read by tunnelling magnetoresistance; zero stray field lets cells touch without crosstalk.
why: Non-volatile (no refresh, fact 3) with ps-scale dynamics and crosstalk-free packing; avoids tungsten/platinum chokepoints. Read signal is still small.

title: Hydrophobic-gating nanopore: wet or vapor-locked pore stores the bit
idea: Many ion channels open and close as water fills or empties a hydrophobic constriction. Seal an array of hydrophobic 1-2 nm nanopores to an electrolyte reservoir. An electric field wets a pore (electrowetting), the wet state persists inside a hysteresis window, and a reverse pulse triggers vapor-lock dewetting; ionic conductance differs by >10^3.
why: Non-volatile bistability with no lattice damage, because the liquid simply refills each cycle; simulations show ns-to-us switching. Built from SiN or graphene membranes.

title: Bulk acoustic delay-line loop memory from RF filter fabs
idea: Worsen: build bits only in scarce DRAM fabs. Flip: store bits as acoustic pulses circulating in short AlN/ScAlN bulk-acoustic delay lines made by RF-filter foundries, with a CMOS regenerator per loop; a $1M, 24-month prototype targets 100 ns loops as a refresh-free buffer.
why: U.S. manufacturability (RF filter fabs are large and US-based), with no capacitor and no refresh; density is modest but capital is tiny.

title: Swap ferromagnet for antiferromagnetic Neel-vector bit with zero stray field
idea: Store the bit in the Neel vector of a non-collinear antiferromagnet (Mn3Sn, Mn3Pt) or of Mn2Au. Neel spin-orbit torque switches it in picoseconds, and it is read through an all-antiferromagnetic tunnel junction (tunnelling magnetoresistance was shown in 2023).
why: Non-volatile, so no refresh (fact 3); immune to field and row-hammer disturbance (fact 9); ps writes. With no dipolar crosstalk, cells pack at litho pitch, which FM MRAM cannot do.

title: Stray-field-free antiferromagnetic tunnel junction bits packed at pitch
idea: Build Mn3Sn/MgO/Mn3Sn all-antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions, where cluster-octupole order gives TMR with no net moment, and write them by spin-orbit torque with ps-scale intrinsic dynamics. With zero stray field, neighbor cells sit at 1-2F spacing without dipolar disturb.
why: Ferromagnetic MRAM density is capped by stray-field coupling; antiferromagnetic order removes it. Aims at sub-ns write and near-4F2 density with no capacitor or refresh (facts 1, 3).

title: Contiguous-disk bubble tracks driven by one global rotating field
idea: Late-1980s bubble chips used ion-implanted contiguous-disk tracks that moved sub-lithographic bubbles under a global rotating in-plane field. On existing 200-mm lines, deposit perpendicular CoTb films, define tracks by ion implantation through a 0.5-um mask (no magnetic etch), drive every track at once with a package-level rotating-field coil, and detect with same-fab magnetoresistive bridges.
why: Bit size set by material (~100 nm) not litho; per-track drivers vanish so periphery shrinks (Fact 7); non-volatile; ~us latency at 10 MHz field makes a capacity tier that offloads DRAM.

title: Nonlinear-permittivity probe reads ferroelectric bits below coercive field
idea: Effect walk: nonlinear dielectric response. The second-order permittivity of a ferroelectric is odd in polarization, so a 50-mV sinusoid far below the coercive voltage produces a second-harmonic charge whose phase flips with the bit; a local lock-in style sense stage reads it while leaving the domain untouched.
why: Turns FeRAM's destructive switch-and-restore read (full coercive CV2) into a 50-mV probe: ~10-20x lower read energy and no read fatigue (fact 8); the small signal needs fF-class cells and local sensing.

title: NiFe-hydrogenase proton loading: hydrogen-doped nickelate Mott switch
idea: Hydrogenase enzymes shuttle protons and electrons in and out of a Ni-Fe active site. Gate a thin SmNiO3 or NdNiO3 channel through a solid proton conductor: a write pulse injects hydrogen, which dopes electrons into the nickelate and drives it from metal to insulator (resistance change >10^3). The hydrogen stays put when unpowered and is pulled back out by reverse bias.
why: Non-volatile, multilevel-capable Mott switch read at low voltage, with large on/off ratio and rare-earth nickelates instead of chalcogenides. Proton moves of a few nm aim at ~100 ns writes.

title: Flip leaky bucket into snap-through buckled nanobeam bit
idea: Worsen: store every bit in a leaky bucket that drains in milliseconds. Flip: store the bit in the shape of a pre-stressed buckled nanobeam (20 nm SiN or SiC) that snaps between two stable states under an electrostatic pulse and is read by the capacitance change to a sense electrode; a shape cannot leak.
why: Kills refresh (fact 3: 16-33% of idle power) and sidesteps the capacitor charge wall (fact 1); fJ-scale writes, unlimited retention, NEMS resonators already show >1e12 cycles.

title: VO2 thermal-hysteresis bit held at hot-water-cooled datacenter temperature
idea: Hot-water-cooled racks run silicon at ~60-65C, inside VO2's insulator-metal hysteresis loop; at that bias temperature a nano-island is bistable, set metallic by a short Joule pulse and reset by a field or cooling pulse, and read by its 100-1000x resistance contrast. The extreme cooling regime itself becomes the storage mechanism.
why: Zero-standby, refresh-free bit with ns switching (fact 3); nanoscale hysteresis width and thermal crosstalk between neighbors are the risks.

title: Three bits per cell via discharge-time encoding and shared TDC
idea: MAGNIFY levels per cell from 2 to 8: the cell discharges into the bitline through a precision current sink and a shared time-to-digital converter measures time-to-threshold (Q = I*t), turning tiny charge differences into ps-resolvable intervals; every refresh re-quantizes levels to cancel drift.
why: 3 bits per capacitor gives ~2.5x cost-per-bit gain net of extra periphery on the existing 6F2 process, no new materials or tools (facts 1, 4).

title: H: proton-intercalated MoO3 cell holds 16 analog levels for AI
idea: Gate a MoO3 channel through a thin phosphosilicate-glass proton electrolyte so each 5 ns pulse inserts a fixed dose of H+, giving 16 conductance levels; AI weights and KV-cache values are stored natively analog, and ~1% level errors are absorbed by the network's own noise tolerance.
why: Four bits per cell with no capacitor and in-place analog reads (facts 1, 5, 8); molybdenum is mined in the U.S.; retention drift and update symmetry are the risks.

title: Qubit-fab double-angle evaporation: self-aligned AlOx overlap storage capacitors
idea: Superconducting-qubit labs make Al/AlOx/Al junctions with one resist bridge and two angled evaporations plus in-situ oxidation; use this Dolan-bridge method to form the storage capacitor and its node contact in one e-beam exposure: first Al leg, controlled O2 dose for a 1.5-3-nm AlOx dielectric, then a second leg at a different angle whose overlap area, not the lithography, sets capacitance.
why: Capital and step count: capacitor plus contact in one exposure with zero overlay error, using an e-beam writer and angle evaporator; low-k AlOx limits charge, so it pairs with gain-cell or avalanche-sensed low-charge cells.

title: Sliding-ferroelectric bilayer hBN: fatigue-free interlayer shift bit
idea: Combine 2D-material stacking with ferroelectric memory: in parallel-stacked bilayer hBN, sliding one layer by a fraction of a lattice constant flips an out-of-plane dipole, and an adjacent MoS2 channel senses the dipole as a threshold shift. Because no bonds break and no ions migrate, switching is reported nearly fatigue-free.
why: Zero refresh with endurance approaching unlimited and sub-ns switching; wafer-scale aligned stacking is the risk.

title: Swap stored charge for snap-through state of buckled nanobeam
idea: A compressively prestressed SiN or diamond-like-carbon nanobeam (~15 x 150 nm) clamped over a recess has two mirror-image buckled states. A 1-2 ns electrostatic pulse from a side electrode snaps it over, and the state is read capacitively without disturbing it.
why: No leakage path, so no refresh (fact 3); non-destructive read removes restore energy (fact 8); immune to radiation and row hammer (fact 9).

title: Molecular quantum-dot cellular automata loop memory
idea: Scale bits down to electron positions inside a 2 nm mixed-valence molecule: the bit is which diagonal pair of four redox sites holds two electrons, and a clocked ring of molecules circulates bits like a shift register.
why: Density and energy: THz switching with near kT energy, theoretical 1e14 bits/cm2.

title: Single-molecule tautomer switch: one hydrogen hop stores a bit
idea: Effect walk: proton tunneling in tautomerization. A porphycene or naphthalocyanine molecule anchored in a nanogap flips which nitrogen atoms hold its inner hydrogens when a 0.2-0.4 eV tunneling electron excites it, and its two tautomers give distinct junction conductance read at 10 mV.
why: Switching costs one vibrational excitation (~0.1 aJ) and a 10-mV, ns read through one molecule is ~10^-17 J: >=100x below DRAM, at molecular density; room-temperature stability and contact reproducibility are speculative.
